title: North Pacific within-type O2 loss peaks on sigma0 26.6-26.7, the classes that stopped outcropping; a pre-set class test fails at the source and GFDL-ESM4 interior O2 does not respond (WOD 1950-2025)
abstract: Question: does the within-water-type oxygen (O2) loss in the North Pacific thermocline follow, class by class, the loss of winter outcrop area of each density class, and does a CMIP6 model show the same pattern? Approach: World Ocean Database ship data (92,520 casts, 1950-2025) on 17 sigma0 classes (25.4-27.0) in 7 regions from 145 E to California; fixed-effects year series with a joint cruise bootstrap; winter outcrop area of each class in 30-50 N, 140 E-150 W from WOD ship and Argo surface data against WOA23; tests written in a plan before the results; the same test in GFDL-ESM4. Results (2009-2025 minus 1984-1996): within-type O2 loss peaks on sigma0 26.6-26.7 in all regions north of 28 N (26.6: -28 umol/kg at 36-46 N, 160 E-180; -22 to -25 from 180 to California; -20 at CalCOFI), while classes 25.4-26.3 lose 0 to -11. AOU rises as O2 falls. The share of winters in which 26.6 outcropped fell from 69% to 6%, and 26.7 from 15% to 0%. At the source the dense-class decline began near 1988-1990 and reached CalCOFI near 2004-2006. The pre-specified fingerprint test failed: correlations of class O2 change with class outcrop change were 0.19, 0.54 and 0.35 in the three test regions (one interval above 0); 0.59-0.76 downstream. Class depth predicts the pattern as well or better (r -0.68 to -0.93). An equivalent density shift of 0.07-0.095 kg/m3 fits the AOU change on 25.4-26.7 (r 0.79-0.96) but over-predicts 26.8-27.0, which never outcropped in the box, so the shift stops below the densest outcropping class. In GFDL-ESM4 the 26.6 outcrop almost vanished (0.149 to 0.015 million km2), but interior O2 on 26.5-26.7 changed by only -3 to +3 umol/kg. Interpretation: the sigma0 26.5 loss studied before is the upper flank of a larger loss on the densest classes that the open North Pacific stopped ventilating; the tested model misses the O2 response, not only the outcrop. Limitations: failed pre-set test; exploratory indices; collinear depth trend; outcrop box excludes the Okhotsk Sea and north of 50 N; few recent cruises at 180-130 W; one model, one member, three sampled years per epoch.

citations.reason: We test its outcrop mechanism class by class and reuse its code and mask: the dense classes lost both outcrop and the most O2 (support), but the pre-set class test failed at its source region and the loss peaks on 26.6-26.7, not 26.5 (challenge).
Its equivalent density shift (0.06-0.105 kg/m3) fits our class shape on 25.4-26.7 with delta 0.07-0.095; we add that the shift stops below the densest outcropping class.
